screens.title: Reviews
screens.label: Review settings
screens.subtitle: Who may review, and the request email

fields.label: Who can review
fields.help: Verified buyers: customers who bought the product, signed in to their account or through the link in their review-request email; their reviews publish right away with a “Verified buyer” badge. Anyone: customers who bought the product still get the badge and publish right away; everyone else gives a name and email (never shown) and waits for your approval.

fields.label: Ask customers for a review
fields.help: One email per order, after it is fulfilled, with a link for each product. Each link works once, for 60 days. Change its wording under Emails → Review request.

fields.label: Send the request (days after fulfillment)
fields.help: Between 3 and 30 days. Give the order time to arrive.

blocks.footer: Verified reviews are published as written, good or bad. You can hide or reject one only for spam, abuse, being off-topic or sharing private information.

screens.title: Taxes
screens.label: Taxes
screens.subtitle: Sales tax rates, lodging and service tax

blocks.text: Choose how this store handles sales tax and save. Until you do, checkout is turned off — we won’t take an order we can’t tax correctly.

fields.label: Calculation
fields.help: Stripe Tax calculates per buyer location at checkout; activate Stripe Tax in your Stripe dashboard first. Don’t collect sales tax: this store adds no sales tax to any order. Orders still go through — the decision is recorded, not the tax.

fields.label: Origin country
fields.help: Where this store ships or sells FROM — the jurisdiction the manual rates are applied from. Not the address your workspace is billed at by Aglyn, and not where your payouts are sent.

blocks.title: Manual rates
blocks.empty: No rates yet. The most specific rate for a destination wins.

blocks.title: Lodging tax

fields.label: Label
fields.help: Shown to the guest on the receipt

blocks.footer: Charged on reservations, on top of the price, using the rate you enter here. It is separate from the sales tax above because occupancy tax is its own regime with its own rates and its own return. Leave it blank to charge none — that is the default. Aglyn applies the rate you enter and records what was charged. It does not determine whether this tax applies to you, at what rate, or where it should be paid — that is yours to decide. On a reservation that takes a deposit, the rate is applied to the deposit — the amount actually charged here — not to the whole stay. If tax is due on the full stay, collect the difference the same way you collect the rest of the balance.

blocks.title: Service tax

fields.label: Label
fields.help: Shown to the client on the receipt

blocks.footer: Charged on paid bookings, on top of the price, using the rate you enter here. It is separate from the sales tax above because whether a service is taxable is often a different question from whether goods are. Leave it blank to charge none — that is the default. Aglyn applies the rate you enter and records what was charged. It does not determine whether this tax applies to you, at what rate, or where it should be paid — that is yours to decide.

screens.title: Payments
screens.label: Payments
screens.subtitle: Your Stripe account and the fee on each sale

blocks.text: Your Stripe account has not been verified for payments on this site, so sales will be refused. Set up payments again to verify it — if it was connected against Stripe test mode, you will need to connect a live account.
Selling requires a paid plan — upgrade on the billing page.

blocks.title: Platform fee on each sale
blocks.footer: Buyers pay on your own Stripe account; Aglyn LLC collects a platform fee per sale based on your plan. Card processing is passed through at cost on top of that: 2.9–6% + 30¢ per online sale, what Stripe charges to take the payment. It is not a Aglyn LLC margin.

blocks.text: Higher plans reduce fees to 0%. The fee is charged on the sale, not on how it was paid — in-person cash and room-charge sales carry it too. On card sales it is deducted from your Stripe payout; on cash and room-charge sales there is no payout to deduct from, so it is added to your monthly Aglyn LLC invoice instead.

methods.label: Apple Pay
methods.requirements: Safari on a Mac, iPhone or iPad with a card in Apple Wallet. Your site’s domain is registered with Apple Pay for you.

methods.label: Google Pay
methods.requirements: Chrome or an Android device with a card saved to Google Pay. With Stripe Tax on, Google Pay shows when the checkout collects a shipping address.

methods.label: Link
methods.requirements: Shoppers who saved a card or bank with Link check out in one step.

methods.label: Klarna
methods.requirements: US shoppers paying in USD. Pay in full, in 30 days, in 4, or monthly financing.
methods.limits: From $10; the highest amount depends on the shopper (financing up to $10,000).

methods.label: Afterpay
methods.requirements: US shoppers paying in USD. Pay in 4 interest-free installments.

methods.label: Affirm
methods.requirements: US shoppers paying in USD. Pay in 4, or monthly installments up to 36 months.

methods.label: Cash App Pay
methods.requirements: US shoppers with Cash App, paying in USD.

methods.label: Amazon Pay
methods.requirements: Shoppers pay with the card and address saved to their Amazon account.

methods.label: Stablecoins (crypto)
methods.requirements: Shoppers pay in USDC or another supported stablecoin from their crypto wallet; you are paid in USD. Refunds go back to the shopper’s wallet as stablecoins, and these payments cannot be disputed.
methods.limits: USD only, up to $10,000 per payment.

blocks.text: Cards are always on. Turn off anything you don’t want to offer. Stripe shows each method only on orders and to shoppers it suits, using the limits below.
Only a site admin can change which payment methods your store offers.

blocks.title: Methods
blocks.filter: item.platform != unavailable && item.platform || item.platform != unavailable && const.methods[id=item.id].kind != crypto

blocks.title: Wallet domains
blocks.footer: Apple Pay shows only on a domain registered with Stripe. Your site’s domains are registered for you when you connect them and on the first in-page checkout.

blocks.text: ShipStation is not available on this site.

Already labeling in ShipStation? Connect it as a Custom Store: ShipStation imports the orders you still have to ship, and each label you buy there marks the order shipped here and emails your customer the tracking link. Only a site admin can connect it.

blocks.title: Paste these into ShipStation
blocks.footer: Anyone with the password can read the name and address on every order you ship. If it gets out, make a new password: the old one stops working at once.

screens.label: ShippingEasy
screens.subtitle: Send orders and take shipments back

blocks.text: ShippingEasy is not available on this site.

Labeling in ShippingEasy? Connect it with the API key, API secret and store API key from your ShippingEasy account: each order is sent there as it is paid, and each label you buy there marks the order shipped here and emails your customer the tracking link. Only a site admin can connect it.

blocks.footer: Paste the callback URL into your API store’s settings in ShippingEasy, so each label marks the order shipped here.

screens.title: Order webhooks
screens.label: Order webhooks
screens.subtitle: Order and return events sent to your own systems

blocks.text: Order webhooks are not set up on this deployment.

blocks.empty: Send order and return events to your own systems — a warehouse, an ERP or a script. Each event is signed so your endpoint can check it came from this store.

prompt.label: Endpoint URL
prompt.help: An https address on a public server. Redirects are not followed.

actions.label: Roll secret
actions.confirm: Roll the signing secret? A new secret signs every event from now on. Update your endpoint before the next order, or it will reject what it is sent.

actions.label: Delete
actions.confirm: Delete {item.url}? It stops receiving order events. Its delivery log is kept for 30 days.

prompt.label: Endpoint URL
prompt.help: An https address on a public server. Redirects are not followed.

blocks.footer: A failed delivery is retried for about a day. Each request carries an Aglyn-Signature header, t=<timestamp>,v1=<signature>. The signature is the HMAC-SHA256, in hex, of the timestamp, a period and the raw body, keyed with the signing secret. Aglyn-Event-Id is the same on every retry.

blocks.empty: No deliveries in the last 30 days.
